canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: Hallow's Creek's chapter of the book of lore, its lines the game's. What they tell of is CANON or CANON-EXPANDED as hallows.json's canonNote says: the paused town, the bridge's slabs, the crater and the red door, the Old Archive and the hungry shadows (book1 ch.15-21), the Hollow (book1 ch.4), the Bureau (book1 ch.3). Written 2026-10-16.

entries.subject: The Ash Road
entries.line: The last road into the town the Wasting took first, its stone trees laying long shadows across it that you should not stand in.
entries.canonStatus: CANON (book1 ch.17: the hungry shadows); GAME-ONLY: the road as a way in

entries.subject: The Fossilised Farm
entries.line: A farmhouse turned to stone with its farmer at the gate and its dog in the yard, the dog sitting up as if someone had just called its name.

entries.subject: The Bridge of Shattered Glass
entries.line: The old bridge was blown apart and the blast stopped mid-air. You cross the chasm on its hanging slabs.

entries.subject: The bridge-head gatehouse
entries.line: Where the Iron Pact holds the bridge's far end for the Bureau.
entries.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the Iron Pact is CANON, book1 ch.2)

entries.subject: Main Street
entries.line: White houses, white fences without a speck of peeling paint, roses of red quartz, a baker in his doorway with a tray, a ball hanging in the air over the gravel. Everyone on it is stone, and watching you.

entries.subject: The Square
entries.line: Where the town hall stood there is a bowl of glass, and a red door hanging over it with nothing to open into.
entries.canonStatus: CANON (book1 ch.19: the crater and the red door; the door is never reached)

entries.subject: The Granary on the race
entries.line: The town's tithe barn, where the Bureau's pickers size what they cut into crates for the coast.
entries.more: The Picker-Master's tally: forty of the paused cut, twelve stone of yield, and a line about the cellars he was told not to number.
entries.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the Bureau is CANON, book1 ch.3)

entries.subject: The Old Archive
entries.line: A First Era library: columns twisted like pulled taffy, a crest of an open book with an eye, a maze of stone shelves. The Preservationists kept it once.
entries.more: A page of the High Archivist's log, found loose in the stacks: the children came to the steps to hear the readings.

entries.subject: The Bell Tower
entries.line: The tower over the town, its great bell hung mid-swing and its painted dial a minute short of noon. Paint on stone: nothing in it turns.
entries.more: Four names chalked low on the inside wall, the ringers' practice marks, the last stopping half way through the word.
entries.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED (book1 ch.21: the tower; the bell, the dial and the ringers GAME-ONLY)

entries.subject: The Cut-Store
entries.line: The cellar where the Bureau's cutters throw what they have broken. What they throw there does not stay thrown.
entries.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the Hollow are CANON, book1 ch.4)

entries.subject: Road-Captain Everard Hurst
entries.line: The Pact captain who keeps the Ash Road for the Bureau's carts and puts anyone in his way down in the ash.

entries.subject: Sergeant Wymond Tredway
entries.line: He holds the gate at the bridge's far end. He says the span is his, and the span has not argued.

entries.subject: Assessor Piers Upcott
entries.line: The Bureau man who walks the street with chalk, marking the paused for the cut. A cross on a door is a cross on a person.

entries.subject: Picker-Master Fulke Yelland
entries.line: He sizes memory-quartz into crates and keeps a tally of everything but what walks after the cut.

entries.subject: First-Cut
entries.line: The first of the paused the Bureau cut. Its shell broke. What was inside it did not go anywhere.
entries.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the Hollow are CANON, book1 ch.4: they pour from cellar doors)

entries.subject: Registrar Dunstan Pardew
entries.line: He keeps the Archive's register for the Bureau now, and says hush to anyone who speaks above a whisper in it.

entries.subject: Bureau Examiner Thurstan Vowell
entries.line: The Examiner learned the town's one trick: a bell rung at the frozen minute wakes the square, and the grey breathes a field wider.

entries.subject: The Lamplighter
entries.line: A Hollow who walks the street at the hour, lighting lamps that give no light. Not every night.
entries.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (the Hollow are CANON, book1 ch.4)

entries.subject: The Old Ram
entries.line: Grey and light as paper, it stood in the east meadow when the meadow went pale. Sometimes it wakes.
entries.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (Bet's letter is already in the game)
